summary: Torkel Brekke works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Oslo under Jens Braarvig and Georg von Simson, and at Oxford under Richard Gombrich, later holding posts at Oxford (~1995–1999) and Oslo (~2001).

Toru Haneda worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1907) and held a post at Kyoto University (~1907–1945), where he taught Yutaka Iwamoto.
Toru Kumeji is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has held positions at the Center for Open Humanities Data and as a chief researcher at the Humanities Information Studies Institute.

Toru Takahashi was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who founded the Koreanology Association. He held professorships at Keijo Imperial University (1926), Fukuoka University (~1947–1950), and Tenri University (~1950–1965).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, serving as an assistant at Lausanne (~1993–2001) and as chief researcher at both the Humanities Information Studies Institute and the Center for Open Humanities Data.

Toshifumi Goto is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1976–1982) under Karl Hoffmann, Gert Klingenschmitt, and Johanna Narten. He was a professor at Osaka University (~1989–1999) and Tohoku University (~1999–2012).
Toshihide Mori is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He held a post as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College.
Toshihide Unebe is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Issai Funahashi. He served as a professor at Doho University.

Toshihiko Izutsu was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Keio University (~1934–1937) and the University of Tokyo, later holding posts at Keio (~1937–1970), McGill University (~1961–1979), and Komazawa University.

Toshihiko Kimura works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1959–1963), where he was later a part-time lecturer, and held positions at Tokai Gakuin University and Shitennoji University as professor emeritus.
Toshihiro Wada is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981. He served as an associate professor at Nagoya University (~1993–2019).

Toshiichi Endo specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and completed his doctoral thesis at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1989–1995) under Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake, later becoming a professor at the University of Hong Kong (~2010).

Toshikazu Watanabe is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~2008), and became a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

Toshiki Osada specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Hokkaido University (~1973–1982) and held positions at the Kyoto University of the Arts and the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2019) as professor and project leader.

Toshinori Ochiai specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He has held positions at Kacho Junior College, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996), and as director at the Research Institute of Old Japanese Manuscripts of Buddhist Scriptures (~1999).
Toshio Ando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1929–1932). He held academic posts at Doho University and Otani University (~1949–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2009) and held research posts at Toyo University (~2012–2020) and Zhejiang University (~2015–2020).

Toshio Nagahiro specialized in history/archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929), where he later served as professor (~1952–1969; emeritus), before holding a post at Kyoto Tachibana University (~1969).
Toshio Sako is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Columbia University (~1989–1996), completing his doctoral studies under Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He held positions at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1949–1957), the University of Tokyo (~1957–1977; emeritus), Chuo University (~1977–1987), and Hannan University.
